name: a100
description: NVIDIA A100 SXM4 (GA100, Ampere, sm_80) at its 1410 MHz boost clock: one Vortex core per SM.

sources.NUM_CORES, NUM_WARPS, NUM_THREADS, ISSUE: 108 SMs, 64 resident warps/SM, 4 schedulers x 32 lanes (NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU Architecture whitepaper, Table 3)
sources.DCACHE_SIZE: 192 KB combined L1/shared per SM (whitepaper), rounded down to the power of two the cache accepts
sources.L2_SIZE, L2_NUM_WAYS, L2_NUM_BANKS: 40 MB L2 in 80 slices (whitepaper), rounded down to 32 MB and 32 banks; 16 ways as in GPGPU-Sim's SM80_A100 dl2
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_TYPE, PLATFORM_MEMORY_NU: 5 HBM2 stacks x 8 128-bit channels = 40 channels at 2430 MT/s, modelled as 32 channels at 3038 MT/s for a power-of-two interleave: 32 x 16 B x 3038 MT/s = 1555 GB/s, the card's bandwidth; the array timing is in nanoseconds, so latency is unchanged
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_LATENCY, PLATFORM_MEMORY: Fixed DRAM latency and per-channel request queue of GPGPU-Sim's SM80_A100 configuration (accel-sim gpu-simulator/configs/tested-cfgs/SM80_A100/gpgpusim.config)
sources.FETCH_WIDTH: 4 SM processing blocks, each with its own warp scheduler, dispatch unit and L0 instruction cache (NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU Architecture whitepaper)
sources.CP_LLC_CLIENT: Host copies reach device memory through the L2 like every other client, so uploaded data is L2-resident at launch
sources.LMEM_LOG_SIZE, DCACHE_SIZE: 164 KB maximum shared memory per SM (CUDA Programming Guide, compute capability 8.0), rounded down to the power of two the LMEM accepts. DCACHE_SIZE keeps the 192 KB L1/shared pool rounded down: the driver gives a kernel the L1 its shared-memory use leaves
sources.LMEM_NUM_BANKS: 32 shared-memory banks of 4 B, as on every NVIDIA GPU since Maxwell (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, shared memory)
sources.VM_ENABLE, EXT_A_ENABLE, EXT_ZACAS_ENABL: Every NVIDIA GPU since Pascal has a demand-paged MMU (unified memory), global and shared-memory atomics with a native compare-and-swap (atomicCAS), FP16 storage and conversion, and per-partition special-function units for the transcendentals (MUFU)
sources.EXT_TCU_ENABLE, TCU_*, EXT_DXA_ENABLE, E: Third-generation tensor cores: FP16/BF16, TF32, INT8 and INT4, with 2:4 structured sparsity (A100 whitepaper). A100 has cp.async but no TMA, so no DXA
sources.xlen: 64-bit machine: 64-bit pointers and FP64 (the D extension follows XLEN=64), with a 48-bit device address space against NVIDIA's 49-bit virtual addresses; configure --profile picks a build64 tree and a build32 tree rejects the profile
sources.NUM_BARRIERS: 16 named CTA barriers (bar.sync 0-15, PTX ISA) on every NVIDIA GPU
sources.EXT_RASTER_ENABLE, EXT_OM_ENABLE: Off: the datacenter part is built for compute (no display outputs; the raster and ROP hardware is reduced or absent), so the profile models its compute machine
sources.NUM_MUFU_LANES: 16 special-function results per clock per SM (4 SFUs in each of the 4 processing blocks) for the reciprocal, reciprocal square root, log2, exp2, sine and cosine (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput, compute capability 8.0)
sources.SIMD_WIDTH: Left at NUM_THREADS (32) although the part has 16 FP32 / 16 INT32 lanes per SM processing block, so a warp instruction issues over two cycles (A100 whitepaper): the RTL TCU needs full-warp operands (NUM_TCU_LANES == NUM_THREADS) and VX_lane_dispatch cannot widen a 16-lane dispatch to 32 lanes, so SIMD_WIDTH=16 with EXT_TCU_ENABLE does not build in rtlsim. The tensor cores are kept; the ALU/FPU/LSU issue width is 2x the part's
